description: Convert dog years to human years with two real methods: the 2019 epigenetic formula (16·ln(age)+31) and the size-based life-stage chart.

faqs.a: human_age = 16 × ln(dog_age) + 31, published by Wang et al. in Cell Systems (2019), based on DNA-methylation comparison of Labrador retrievers and humans. It is not a straight multiplier — dogs age fast early, then slow down.
faqs.q: What is the epigenetic dog-age formula?

faqs.a: Small breeds age slowest per year: 1 yr = 15, 2 yrs = 24, then ≈ +4/yr. Large breeds age fastest: 6 yrs ≈ 45, 10 yrs ≈ 66. Pick your dog's size to see the difference.
faqs.q: Why do the two methods give different answers?

faqs.a: Yes — the size chart shows big dogs age faster per year, while the single epigenetic curve is breed-averaged. Presenting both lets you compare.

howto: Enter your dog's age in years (decimals allowed, e.g. 2.5).
Pick your dog's size class (small, medium or large).
Compare the epigenetic formula result with the size-based chart result and life stage.
title: Dog Age Converter
